title: Education Why Learn to Write Essays When AI Can Do It for Us? Matthews, Paul
author: Matthews, Paul
summary: High school teacher Paul Matthews grapples with the most fundamental challenge AI poses to education: if students can generate essays with AI, what justification remains for teaching them to write? Matthews approaches the question from a classroom perspective, working with students navigating anxiety about their futures in an AI-saturated world. He argues the answer lies in understanding what essay writing actually develops beyond the essay itself: cognitive operations of clarifying thinking, ordering evidence, locating logical gaps, and sustaining concentration that are valuable regardless of whether the output has practical use. Matthews also argues that the human capacity to connect rigorous thinking to students' sense of identity and personal stakes -- grounded in relationship rather than information transfer -- is precisely what AI cannot replicate. The article is an honest teacher-on-the-ground reflection rather than a policy argument.
points: The surface justification for essay writing -- demonstrating knowledge and communication skill -- is largely undermined by AI, but the deeper justification -- developing cognitive habits of ordering evidence and sustaining an argument -- remains valid and is more important in an AI-rich environment.

Students who use AI to bypass writing are bypassing the cognitive work that would build the very capabilities AI cannot replace -- the capacity to evaluate AI outputs critically and to judge when an argument is actually good.

Teachers' comparative advantage over AI is relational, not informational: they can connect the demand for rigorous thinking to a student's sense of identity, future, and personal stakes in a way no tool can.

Education is not primarily the transmission of content that could be delivered more efficiently by software, but the guided development of cognitive and personal capacities that require a human relationship to anchor.

Schools that fail to articulate why they teach what they teach -- beyond 'AI can't do this yet' -- have no stable ground to stand on, because AI capabilities will keep expanding and only a principled account of human development can outlast them.
